text:
sophia: quick heads-up — onboarding weights for `llama3-small-v2` are uploaded to gs://redwood-weights/onboard/llama3-small-v2. when I ran the tokenizer against the chat template we use, I'm seeing an extra BOS token inserted by the runtime. not sure if model card or runtime config is at fault :thinking_face:

raj: can you paste a tiny example (raw string -> token ids)? sometimes the model's special token names differ (`<s>` vs `<|bos|>`).

sophia: yep. example input and tokenization (local tokenizer binary):

```
input = "User: Tell me a joke\nAssistant:"
tokens = tokenizer.encode(input)
# output ids
tokens -> [1002, 58, 72, 9, 400, 2]
# tokenizer.special_tokens_map -> {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>"}
```

sophia: runtime (redwood-serving) logs show we prepend a BOS at serve-time, so request arriving to model actually looks like: `<s>` + encoded_tokens -> leading to double-bos semantics.

mike: that double-BOS can shift kv-cache indexing and cause generation start to repeat or drop first token. EMILY, did we have a recent change to `prepend_bos` behavior in the tokenizer adapter?

emily: I pushed a change last month to make adapter follow model_card.prepend_bos if present. model card for this weights bundle is missing `prepend_bos` right now. oops.

raj: easy fix: add "prepend_bos": false to the model card if the weights expect the tokenizer to already include it, or set it to true if model expects runtime to add it. which is the native behavior of these weights?

sophia: upstream checkpoints were saved with the tokenizer already containing `<s>`. so runtime should NOT add another one. setting `prepend_bos: false` in model card sounds right.

mike: I'll open a tiny PR to the model metadata repo with the model_card patch + a quick unit test that checks token length parity between tokenizer.encode and runtime.prepended sequence.

raj: assign to @mike please and ping me for review. tiny checklist: (1) add prepend_bos:false, (2) document special_token mapping (bos->"<s>"), (3) add a hermetic tokenizer smoke test.

mike: will do. PR draft in a few mins. also adding a CI job that runs the token parity test against the runtime docker image we use in nightly.

ops-bot: deploy preview started for branch mike/model-card/prepend-bos-fix — build 4821.

sophia: thank you. once PR lands can someone run a quick integration against the onboard GPU pool? I want to validate streaming behavior and that EOS comes through as expected. sample curl we'll use:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/infer" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"llama3-small-v2","input":"User: Tell me a joke\nAssistant:","stream":true}'
```

mike: will run on dedicated pool after deploy preview passes. I'll post results here.

emily: small note: also watch out for chat template trimming — some templates add trailing whitespace/newline which changes tokenization for certain tokenizers (off-by-one). I added a trim step in the adapter, but it's gated behind `normalize_whitespace: true` in model card. maybe add that too.

sophia: good catch. include `normalize_whitespace: true` in the model card update then.

raj: tagging this as a serving-readiness item. SOP: model-card update + CI token parity test + integration run on onboard dedicated pool + ack from eng-ml.

deploy-bot: preview deploy completed for build 4821 — all tests green :white_check_mark:

mike: ran the integration on dedicated pool — streaming tokens look good, no duplicate BOS, EOS token present at end. sample verify output:

```
received_tokens -> [1002, 58, 72, 9, 400, 2]  # matches tokenizer.encode
eos_seen -> true
```

sophia: awesome — thanks everyone :raised_hands: please leave the PR link when ready and I'll mark onboarding complete in the tracker.

raj: reviewed and approved. :shipit:

mike: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/277 — contains model_card changes + unit test.

sophia: marking in tracker. closing the loop. :eyes:
